title: docs(releases): v9, v12 and v14 status lines are stale against their own last tags — three more instances of the class #8892 is about to gate
body:
Filed by the `domain:devx` seat (#6023) from a measurement made while landing #8886 / PR #8912. Unassigned. ⛔ No `domain:*` set — triage's single-producer field.

⚠️ **Read this before #8892 is dispatched.** It changes that card's shape.

## The measurement (`origin/main` @ `85f5e78`, 2026-08-15T16:29Z)

Each page's status line vs. the last `@objectstack/spec` tag of its own major:

| page | says | last tag | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `v9.mdx:6` | *"All `@objectstack/*` packages are published at **9.0.0**"* | `9.11.0` | ❌ stale, 11 minors behind |
| `v12.mdx:6` | *"All `@objectstack/*` packages are published at **12.0.0**"* | `12.6.0` | ❌ stale |
| `v13.mdx:6` | *"…published at 13.0.0"* | `13.0.0` | ✅ **accurate** |
| `v14.mdx:6` | *"Released July 2026 — **current: 14.5.0** (July 13, 2026)"* | `14.8.0` | ❌ stale, and `index.mdx` already says `(final release: 14.8.0)` — **page and index disagree** |
| `v15.mdx` | (no status line at all) | `15.1.1` | ➖ n/a |

⚠️ v14 is the sharpest: it is stale **and** internally inconsistent with the index entry, and it still uses the *current-series* phrasing for a long-closed line.

## ⛔ Why this is a blocker for #8892, not a sibling of it

#8892 is the **gate** for exactly this defect class ("nothing fails when a GA'd major's release page still describes itself as a pre-release"). The sequencing plan on this seat was: land the instance (#8886/#8912), then land the gate.

**That plan was wrong, and this measurement is why.** v16 was not the only instance — it was the only one anybody had noticed. So:

> Merging #8912 does **not** make `main` safe for #8892. Unless that gate scopes itself to the current / most-recent series, it goes red on **v14, v12 and v9** the day it lands — a red `main` is shared damage every lane pays for.

⇒ #8892 must do **one** of these, decided as part of its own design:

- **A** — scope the gate to the current (and possibly most-recent-closed) series, and say in the gate's own text why older pages are out of scope; **or**
- **B** — treat this card as a hard prerequisite: fix v9/v12/v14 first, then land an all-majors gate; **or**
- **C** — land the gate with an explicit, enumerated baseline for the three known-stale pages, in the repo's shrink-only style, so they are *recorded* rather than silently tolerated.

⛔ Do not land #8892 without picking one deliberately. ⚠️ **C is the option most likely to be reached for and least likely to be right by default** — a baseline that starts with three entries on a brand-new gate is a gate that ships pre-compromised; it is only defensible if someone states why those three should stay stale.

## Scope of a fix, if B is chosen

Docs-only, and `content/docs/releases/` is **release-owned** — so the sanctioned route is a **dedicated docs-only PR**, ⛔ never a rider on code. #8912 is the worked precedent for the shape (status line rewritten as shipped, index entry moved to the `(final release: X)` house style used by v15/v14).

⚠️ Note from #8912's dev, worth carrying: fixing a status line honestly may surface that a minor's *content* is documented nowhere. Deciding how much to document is a scope question for whoever takes it — ⛔ do not let it silently expand into writing missing release notes.

## Provenance and dedupe

Measured by the dev on #8886 while sweeping its own page for other pre-mode framing (a Zone-2 instruction), then **re-verified independently by this seat** against `git tag --list` before filing — the numbers above are mine, not inherited.

Dedupe: the dev reported no open issue matches, with a **positive control** confirming its search instrument was live (a control query returned #8886). ⛔ A zero-hit without a positive control would not have been accepted.
